title: Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection
authors: Tsung-Yi Lin, Priya Goyal, Ross Girshick, Kaiming He, Piotr Dollár
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
conclusions: Identifies extreme foreground-background class imbalance during one-stage dense-detector training as the central obstacle to matching two-stage detector accuracy.

Proposes the focal loss FL(p_t) = -(1-p_t)^gamma log(p_t), a modulating factor added to cross-entropy that down-weights well-classified ('easy') examples and focuses training on hard examples, with an alpha-balanced variant.

Introduces RetinaNet, a simple one-stage detector (ResNet-FPN backbone + class/box subnets) trained with focal loss, which for the first time matches/surpasses state-of-the-art two-stage detector accuracy on COCO while retaining one-stage speed.
Shows focal loss outperforms alternatives to class-imbalance handling such as alpha-balanced CE and online hard example mining (OHEM) by ~3 AP points.

Notes the precise functional form of focal loss is not crucial (an alternate FL* form works comparably), and studies model initialization (prior pi) as important for training stability under imbalance.
our_use: main.tex:207-213, paragraph 'Cost-sensitive and imbalanced training': cited alongside elkan2001foundations, cui2019class, cao2019learning, menon2021logit as one of several loss-reshaping/reweighting approaches to class imbalance, with the point that 'None of it guarantees the prediction count; the realized number of constrained-class predictions remains a free outcome.'
